records.subject: Late rare-earth substitution in (Ca1-xRx)3Co2O6

records.quote: In this study, using commercial cotton fabric, we created efficient thermoelectric (TE) textile that, unlike analogs, is based on thin-film composite of biocompatible semiconductor copper iodide (CuI) and biodegradable polymer nanocellulose (NCp) obtained by processing a widespread plant common reed.

record.subject: Textile-based thermoelectric generators
record.object: Biomedical and consumer health and safety applications
record.conditions: Attributed jointly to inherent flexibility and wearability
record.quote: Due to the inherent flexibility and wearability features, textile-based thermoelectric generators (TEGs) possess significant potential for biomedical and consumer health and safety applications.

record.subject: CuI film
record.quote: The NCp sublayer made it possible to fabricate thin-film ohmic contacts through vacuum deposition of chromium on the nanostructured CuI film in the TE textile.
